article.title: NFL EDGE Friday Evening Brief
article.dek: Final injury news sharpens Cincinnati-Houston while the Week 2 card holds its core recommendations.

items.headline: Houston loses Collins; Burrow finishes the week full
paragraphs: Houston receiver Nico Collins is out Sunday with a hamstring injury, and Jadeveon Clowney is also out. Cincinnati quarterback Joe Burrow returned to a full practice Friday but carries a questionable designation; Bengals coach Zac Taylor said Burrow should be good to play.

For Kansas City, Josh Simmons and Chamarri Conner are out Sunday night. Chris Jones is questionable after another limited practice, while Patrick Mahomes practiced fully all week. Indianapolis quarterback Anthony Richardson practiced fully Friday and will serve as the backup.

sections.title: What It Means for NFL EDGE

items.headline: Cincinnati remains the news-sensitive recommendation
paragraphs: Cincinnati remains +2.5 at DraftKings -102, Play Through -105, for 1.0 unit. Collins being ruled out strengthens the reason to pay attention to the matchup, while Burrow's full Friday practice removes some of the uncertainty we had this morning. Neither update is permission to pay beyond the NFL EDGE price ceiling.
Kansas City remains the Hit Rate play, but its price moved the wrong direction tonight to -290 with Play Through -301.

items.headline: Cincinnati has an interesting disagreement, but not a clean Fade
paragraphs: Current DraftKings data displayed by VSiN shows 60% of spread tickets on Cincinnati but only 17% of the spread money. Put simply: more individual bets prefer Cincinnati while a much larger share of dollars is landing on Houston.

VSiN's broader line tracker also shows several books around Cincinnati +1.5 rather than the +2.5 captured by NFL EDGE. That movement toward Cincinnati despite the DraftKings money concentration on Houston is worth noticing, but without a fresh verified Circa split it is not enough to label this a sharp-versus-public Fade.
items.takeaway: If DraftKings still offers the NFL EDGE Cincinnati +2.5 at -105 or better, stay with the card. Do not accept +1.5 just because the wider market moved there, and do not pay beyond Play Through.

items.headline: Cincinnati holds; Kansas City gets more expensive
paragraphs: The newest canonical publication is publication-b18b295053bd7d7a3ee9f186, observed at 2026-09-19T00:08:04Z. Compared with the immediately preceding morning publication, Balanced remains Cincinnati +2.5 at DraftKings -102 with Play Through -105 for 1.0 unit. Value remains the same exact Cincinnati offer and remains suppressed as a duplicate of Balanced for portfolio staking.
Hit Rate remains Kansas City moneyline, but its price worsened from -285 with Play Through -296 to -290 with Play Through -301. No recommendation disappeared, returned, or changed lanes tonight.
items.takeaway: The Cincinnati recommendation is stable. Kansas City is the same play at a worse price, so use the current Play Through rather than an older guardrail.

items.headline: A better number matters more than being five minutes faster
paragraphs: If your app says +2.5 and another screen says +1.5, those are not interchangeable bets. That full point can decide whether you win, push, or lose. Check the actual sportsbook offer before submitting the wager, and if the NFL EDGE number is gone, do not pretend you are still making the same bet.
